issue.title: refactor(comments): split comments_bloc.dart into three focused blocs
issue.body:
## Description

Carves the 1,462-line `CommentsBloc` into three focused successor blocs composed via `MultiBlocProvider`, with cross-bloc coordination going through `BlocListener`-bridged outbox signals per `.claude/rules/state_management.md`'s no-BLoC-to-BLoC dependency rule.

### Successor blocs (each under 500 lines)

| Bloc | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `CommentsListBloc` | **497** | Canonical `commentsById` store, load / paginate / sort / real-time stream / EOSE tracking, plus six new store-mutation events received from the two other blocs' outbox signals (`OptimisticCommentInserted`/`Confirmed`/`RolledBack`, `CommentReplacedInStore`, `CommentRemovedFromStore`, `CommentsRemovedByAuthorFromStore`). |
| `CommentComposerBloc` | **498** | Main / reply / edit input state, two-tier mention search (`restartable()`), publish + edit publish flows; emits `ComposerOutbox{Insert,Confirm,Rollback}Placeholder` / `ReplaceComment` for the UI to bridge into list-bloc store mutations. |
| `CommentReactionsBloc` | **388** | Vote / vote-counts fetch / report / block / delete with `droppable()` transformers; emits `ReactionsOutbox{RemoveComment,RemoveByAuthor}` for list cleanup after block + delete. |

### Outbox bridging

`_OutboxBridges` in `comments_screen.dart` wires two `BlocListener`s that translate composer / reactions outbox state changes into `CommentsListBloc` events, then dispatches `ComposerOutboxConsumed` / `ReactionsOutboxConsumed` to clear the signal. The bridge also re-dispatches `CommentVoteCountsFetchRequested` onto `CommentReactionsBloc` whenever the loaded comment set changes (replaces the previous self-add inside `CommentsBloc._onLoadRequested`).

### Helper extractions (pure-Dart, no bloc dependency)

To keep each bloc under the issue's 500-line acceptance criterion:

- `comments_list/throttled_subscription.dart` — token-bucket stream listener + auto-cancelling subscription wrapper.
- `comments_list/comments_list_helpers.dart` — `commentEngagementScore` + `computeReplyCounts`.
- `comment_composer/mention_search.dart` — tier-1 local + tier-2 REST mention search returning plain records so the bloc owns the user-facing `MentionSuggestion` type.

### #4478 cache-key fix preserved

`rootAddressableId` is injected into all three blocs at construction. Every `postComment` / `deleteComment` / `loadComments` call site verifies the addressable-id thread-through via `verify()` (three explicit "(#4478)" tests in the new bloc test files). Three new outbox-emission tests guard the optimistic-placeholder reconciliation including the relay-echo-arrives-first race that `_onNewCommentReceived` resolves by matching placeholder by author+content.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Verification

- `flutter test test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — **133/133 pass**, including 17 reactions tests, 20 composer tests, 24 list-bloc tests, and 72 widget tests covering the new `MultiBlocProvider` tree.
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — **0 issues**.
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed lib/blocs/comments/ lib/screens/comments/ test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — clean.
- `wc -l` each successor bloc:
  - `comments_list_bloc.dart` — 497 lines
  - `comment_composer_bloc.dart` — 498 lines
  - `comment_reactions_bloc.dart` — 388 lines

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Open comments sheet on a NIP-71 addressable video → list loads.
- [ ] Type and send a comment → placeholder appears immediately; settles to real id on relay echo.
- [ ] Edit own comment → original removed and replacement appears in-place.
- [ ] Delete own comment → row disappears.
- [ ] Block another user → all their comments disappear from the open sheet.
- [ ] Upvote / downvote / switch / remove vote → net score updates optimistically, reverts on relay failure.
- [ ] Report a comment → no list mutation, no error toast.
- [ ] Cycle sort modes (New → Top → Old → New) → engagement sort reads upvote counts from reactions bloc through `comments_list.dart`'s nested `BlocSelector`.
- [ ] Edit a video that has ≥1 comment → re-open from profile → comment count does not drop to 0 (preserves #4478 cache fix).

## Acceptance criteria (from #4516)

- [x] Each successor bloc is under 500 lines. (497 / 498 / 388)
- [x] Existing comment widget tests pass after the split (provider-tree updated to `MultiBlocProvider`).
- [x] Cache-key fix from #4478 (addressable-edit dedup) is preserved.

Closes #4516

review.body: Requesting changes because this patch still has correctness regressions in the editor timeline coordinate mapping and in the editor/export duration contract. The per-clip speed model is directionally right, but before merge this needs: (1) all global-timeline -> clip-local conversions updated to playback-time offsets, not source-time trimmed durations; (2) the speed UI/editor constrained so it cannot compose past the 6.3 s render cap, or the export path changed to match the new timeline contract; and (3) the Linux backend finished so seek/state math uses playback-time offsets consistently. Also worth fixing in this PR: the unexpected upload fallback path still drops playbackSpeed.

comment.body: This only adds per-clip speed selection; the backend's duration/offset math is still in source time. `seekTo`, `_rebuildClipOffsets`, `_totalDuration`, and `_refreshState` continue to use raw clip durations/current positions, so Linux timeline position, scrubbing, and total duration drift as soon as any clip is not `1.0x`. Since this PR changes the shared model/timeline contract to playback time, the Linux backend needs the same coordinate-space conversion before merge.

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -592,6 +592,7 @@ class VideoEditorRenderService {
                 startTime: c.trimStart == .zero ? null : c.trimStart,
                 endTime: c.trimStart + c.trimmedDuration,
                 volume: c.volume,
+                playbackSpeed: c.playbackSpeed,
comment.body: Propagating `playbackSpeed` into the render segments is necessary, but the editor state now reports total duration in playback time while `_concatenateSegments` still hard-caps the final render to `VideoEditorConstants.maxDuration`. That means the editor can represent a composition that export will cut off. Please either clamp/disallow speed edits that push playback duration past the render cap, or update the export contract so the editor and renderer agree.

This listener updates native playback speed, but there are still source-time assumptions elsewhere in this file. `_consumeTrimEndStartPosition` above still accumulates preceding clips with `trimmedDuration`, so after adjusting speeds on earlier clips the post-trim seek target can jump to the wrong global position. The timeline/player contract needs to be playback-time end-to-end, not just in the geometry helpers and native player calls.

Adding per-clip speed here changes the timeline's coordinate space, but the split path later in this file still derives `clipStart` by summing `trimmedDuration`. Once any earlier clip is sped up or slowed down, the playhead's global position no longer maps to the selected clip's source timeline correctly, so split lands on the wrong frame. This needs to be converted to playback-time offsets before merge.

comment.body: This test helper mirrors the production screen structure instead of pumping the real production wiring, so it bypasses `_OutboxBridges` entirely. That leaves the main integration seam introduced by the split untested: if the bridge listeners, `listenWhen` predicates, or `...OutboxConsumed()` dispatches break, these tests still stay green. Please add at least one widget test that exercises the real bridge path.

`copyWith` currently clears `error` on every call unless the caller re-passes it. That works with the current listener flow, but it is inconsistent with the other two blocs and easy to misuse later. Please either align this with the `clearError` pattern used elsewhere or make the semantics explicit so routine state updates do not silently drop errors.

This introduces new user-visible English strings plus an unlinked TODO in the UI mapping layer. Per the repo rules and the localization guidance, this should either be wired through `context.l10n` now or backed by a linked tracking issue if it truly cannot be finished in this PR. Given the refactor already converted bloc errors to enums, the remaining UI mapping work is mechanical and should stay in-scope here.

- release bump PRs update all shipped iOS bundle version metadata consistently
- PR descriptions can truthfully say the iOS build inputs were refreshed
- tracked backup artifacts are removed from the repo when encountered in this path

- Handle expected repository and domain failures in typed on Exception catch blocks.
- Add a trailing generic catch path for unexpected failures and wrap those with Reportable(...) at the addError call site.

## Description

classified each of the 6 `addError(` sites in `NotificationFeedBloc` as

[`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#decision-matrix)
are matrix-YES.

This PR narrows each catch into two arms:

- `on Exception catch (e, s)` — matrix-NO domain failures, behavior
  unchanged (PR #4599 classification comment preserved verbatim).
- `catch (e, s)` — matrix-YES invariant violations, wrapped with
  `Reportable(e, context: NotificationFeedBlocReportableSites.xxx)` so
  `DivineBlocObserver` forwards them to Crashlytics. Recovery emit
  mirrors the matrix-NO arm so UX is preserved.

6 Reportable wraps > 2-site threshold → new
`mobile/lib/notifications/bloc/reportable_sites.dart` with stable
constants (per the lift-into-constants rule).

| # | Site (line) | Method | Repo call | matrix-NO arm sees | matrix-YES constant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_onStarted` | `refresh()` | `FunnelcakeException` (retried 5xx/timeout) | `onStarted` | |
| 2 | `_onLoadMore` | `getNotifications()` | `FunnelcakeException` (single-attempt) | `onLoadMore` | |
| 3 | `_onRefreshed` | `refresh()` | `FunnelcakeException` | `onRefreshed` | |
| 4 | `_onItemTapped` | `markAsRead()` | `FunnelcakeException`, Drift `SqliteException` | `onItemTapped` | |
| 5 | `_onMarkAllRead` | `markAllAsRead()` | `FunnelcakeException`, Drift `SqliteException` | `onMarkAllRead` | |

issue.title: Search: support server-backed video sorting with stable pagination
issue.body:
## Problem
Video search currently relies on local ordering and does not expose server-backed sort modes. That creates three concrete product issues:

- users cannot explicitly change how video search results are ranked
- progressive search / pagination can reorder or append stale results when the sort changes mid-request
- fullscreen playback can jump away from the active video when refreshed search results prepend or reshuffle items

## Goal
Ship server-backed video sorting for the Videos search filter and make the app preserve server ranking consistently across repository, bloc, and fullscreen-feed updates.

## Scope
- switch video search API calls to the server-backed search endpoint with `type=video`, `sort`, and cursor pagination support
- expose the supported sort modes in app state and the Videos search UI
- preserve API result order when combining local and remote search results
- prevent stale search-stream and load-more responses from one sort from mutating the state for another sort
- preserve the current fullscreen video by ID when result ordering changes
- cover the behavior with repository, bloc, widget, and fullscreen-feed tests

## Acceptance Criteria
- when the active search filter is Videos, the UI shows a sort control next to the filter pill
- selecting a sort reruns the current query with the new server-backed sort
- pagination uses the same selected sort and does not append results from an older in-flight sort
- repository-level progressive search keeps API-ranked results ahead of local fallback results without re-sorting them by legacy loops/time logic
- fullscreen feed stays pinned to the same video ID across reordered result updates when that video is still present
- localization copy for the new sort options is present and test-covered

## Non-goals
- adding new search types beyond videos
- changing profile search behavior
- redesigning the broader search screen layout beyond the video sort affordance

## Verification
- focused API client, repository, bloc, widget, fullscreen-feed, and localization tests pass
- `flutter analyze` passes for the touched areas
- manual device verification confirms the dual-pill layout fits on narrow screens

- progressive search / pagination can reorder or append stale results when the sort changes mid-request
- fullscreen playback can jump away from the active video when refreshed search results prepend or reshuffle items

## Goal
Ship server-backed video sorting for the Videos search filter and make the app preserve server ranking consistently across repository, bloc, and fullscreen-feed updates.

## Scope
- switch video search API calls to the server-backed search endpoint with `type=video`, `sort`, and cursor pagination support
- expose the supported sort modes in app state and the Videos search UI
- preserve API result order when combining local and remote search results
- prevent stale search-stream and load-more responses from one sort from mutating the state for another sort
- preserve the current fullscreen video by ID when result ordering changes
- cover the behavior with repository, bloc, widget, and fullscreen-feed tests

## Acceptance Criteria
- when the active search filter is Videos, the UI shows a sort control next to the filter pill
- selecting a sort reruns the current query with the new server-backed sort
- pagination uses the same selected sort and does not append results from an older in-flight sort
- repository-level progressive search keeps API-ranked results ahead of local fallback results without re-sorting them by legacy loops/time logic
- fullscreen feed stays pinned to the same video ID across reordered result updates when that video is still present
- localization copy for the new sort options is present and test-covered

## Non-goals
- adding new search types beyond videos
- changing profile search behavior
- redesigning the broader search screen layout beyond the video sort affordance

## Verification
- focused API client, repository, bloc, widget, fullscreen-feed, and localization tests pass
- `flutter analyze` passes for the touched areas
- manual device verification confirms the dual-pill layout fits on narrow screens

issue.title: feat: document CAWG "do not train" assertion as Divine policy (and remove the unused opt-in path)
issue.body:
### What would you like?

Document our existing CAWG `training-mining` assertion — embedded in the C2PA metadata of every published video — as **Divine policy**, not as a toggleable default. And remove the unused opt-in code path so it's truly the only option.

Current state on `main`:
- `C2paSigningService` embeds a `cawg.training-mining` assertion marking `ai_training`, `ai_inference`, `ai_generative_training`, and `data_mining` as `notAllowed`.
- `AiTrainingPreferenceService.isOptOutEnabled` defaults to `true` and is read by the publish / edit / clip providers.
- A `setOptOutEnabled(false)` API exists in the service but has no caller and no UI surface.

What's missing:
1. **User-facing docs** that say plainly: every video uploaded through Divine carries a cryptographically signed assertion opting the content out of AI training and data mining. This is policy, not a setting.
2. **Code hygiene** — remove `AiTrainingPreferenceService.setOptOutEnabled(false)` and the `aiTrainingOptOut: false` branches so the assertion is unconditional. Either keep the service as a thin always-on sentinel or inline the constant at the call sites.
3. **Coverage audit** — confirm every upload path embeds the assertion (camera record → publish, video editor → publish, clip → publish, plus any web / repost paths).

### How would this be useful for you?

Two reasons:

1. **Creator clarity.** Creators picking Divine should know that uploading here automatically attaches a CAWG-compliant "do not train" signal to their content. That's a meaningful trust signal vs. platforms that either don't mark content or bury the toggle.
2. **Transparent framing.** Like `robots.txt` or "do not track," the assertion will be ignored by bad actors. The value isn't technical prevention — it's a cryptographically signed line in the sand. The docs should say that plainly rather than overpromise.

Keeping it as "the only option" matters: if Divine ever exposes an opt-in toggle, the signal weakens for every other Divine creator (bad actors can then argue ambiguity). Unconditional protects everyone uploading here.

### When would you use this?

- New creators evaluating Divine want to know what protections their content carries.
- Press / partner / legal conversations where we need to point to a written policy.
- Inevitable "why doesn't Divine let me opt in to training?" support questions — we want one clear answer to link.

### Anything else?

Spec we follow: [CAWG Training and Data Mining v1.1](https://cawg.io/training-and-data-mining/1.1/)

Existing implementation pointers:
- `mobile/lib/services/c2pa_signing_service.dart` — manifest builder
- `mobile/lib/services/ai_training_preference_service.dart` — to be simplified or removed
- `mobile/lib/providers/video_publish_provider.dart`, `video_editor_provider.dart`, `clip_manager_provider.dart` — call sites
- `mobile/test/services/c2pa_training_mining_assertion_test.dart` — existing tests; the "excludes assertion when opt-out disabled" case will need to be inverted to "always includes assertion"

Out of scope for this issue:
- Server-side enforcement or re-signing of older content
- Surfacing the assertion in an in-app metadata viewer (possible follow-up)
- Coordinating with relays / other Nostr clients on honoring the assertion

review.body: LGTM. This is an excellent simplification of the creation stack. By moving to an unconditional CAWG assertion, we Establish a clear platform policy while simultaneously purging the technical debt of per-user toggle logic and state hydration for AI preferences. Approved.
